title: External linkage and variable forward declarations
recap: Identifiers with external linkage can refer to the same entity from different translation units. A variable used from another source file needs a matching extern declaration with no initializer at the point of use.

A non-const global variable has external linkage by default, while a const global needs extern on its initialized definition to override its default internal linkage. Exactly one translation unit should provide each non-inline definition.
objectives: Define one non-const global with external linkage.
Define one const global with external linkage.
Forward declare both variables with extern in another source file.
Use the linked variables in a calculated result.
warnings: An extern declaration without an initializer is not a definition and must be matched by a definition elsewhere.
Do not put extern on an initialized non-const definition; it is redundant and may trigger a warning.
A const global definition needs extern if it must be visible from another translation unit.
challenge: In limits.cpp, define g_dailyLimit as 12 without extern and define the const g_bonusLimit as 3 with extern. Forward declare both variables in main.cpp, add them, and print the daily capacity.
hints: The non-const definition is int g_dailyLimit{ 12 };.
The const definition needs an initializer and external linkage: extern const int g_bonusLimit{ 3 };.
In main.cpp, both forward declarations use extern but neither has an initializer.
